explanation: In Italy, tipping is not mandatory or expected as service charge (coperto) is usually included in the bill. Leaving a small amount (5-10%) is seen as a generous gesture for exceptional service, but overtipping can be awkward or mistaken for ignorance.
local_tip: Round up the bill or leave a few euros in cash on the table, but never tip more than 10%.
regional_note: In tourist-heavy areas (Rome, Venice, Florence) tipping is more common and accepted, while in smaller towns or the south it may be less expected.

also_check.note: Tipping is considered insulting; excellent service is the norm.
Tipping 15-20% is standard and expected for service staff.
Service is included, but leaving small change is appreciated for good service.
